Design finding (documented in-file, section note before modalApplyOne_fst_eq_of_not_box): modalApplyOne's propositional dispatch (tryAllPropRules) has priority and is exhaustive over every `.imp _ _`-shaped formula (modalNegOf? unconditionally matches `.imp a .bot`). Consequence: the Lukasiewicz-encoded diamond patterns (`.pos`/`.neg, .imp (.box (.imp _ .bot)) .bot`) are ALWAYS decoded as a propositional negation rule, never reaching the branch/acc-dependent diamondPos/diamondNeg arms of modalApplyOne's modal-rule match (Rules.lean:91,142) -- those arms are dead code in practice. Only `.pos,.box _` (boxPos, persistent) and `.neg,.box _` (boxNeg, linear/fresh-world) ever reach the modal dispatch. This resolves an initial concern that a naive port of classicalStepBranch_hintikka_inv would be unprovable for diamond-typed formulas (it isn't an issue in practice, but IS a real reason boxNeg specifically must be excluded from the invariant's scope -- matching modalHintikkaSet's own conjunct-2 carve-out).

modalStepBranch_hintikka_inv's invariant/conclusion is expressed via a new private def `modalHintikkaClause s φ w X Y` (rather than repeating the inline `match φ with | .box _ => True | _ => match (modalApplyOne ...) ...` at each use site) -- an inline-match version triggered a Lean dependent-match elaboration mismatch (`match φ, hInv with ...` vs `match sf.formula with ...`) when the same clause shape was used as both a hypothesis in one lemma and a goal in another. Naming the clause as a def gave a single shared matcher and resolved it cleanly.

modalStepBranch_hintikka_inv's conclusion is stated over `newBs.zip newExps` pairs (rather than assuming a fixed correspondence) since modalStepBranch's branching arm produces newExps as `branches.map (fun _ => e ++ [sf])` -- a constant list, not obviously index-matched without the zip.
